source.title: Agents omit HTTP status from MCP warnings and tool errors

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
The standalone Agents SDK loses HTTP status codes when it formats MCP failures for connection warnings, verification results and tool-call errors.

This affects `@n8n/agents`, including agents configured through the Agents interface. #44145 and #44146 cover the separate workflow MCP Client nodes.

### Reproduction

Use an MCP server that supports Streamable HTTP. Return HTTP 429 or HTTP 503 with the same response body, `Unavailable`, during initialization, `tools/list` or `tools/call`.

1. Call `McpClient.listTools()` and inspect `getConnectionFailures()`.
2. Call `McpClient.verify()` and inspect its errors.
3. Let an agent call a discovered MCP tool and inspect the rejected tool result sent to the next model turn.

Both statuses produce the same text:

```text
Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint: Unavailable
```

The MCP transport exception still has `code: 429` or `code: 503`. The status disappears when n8n keeps only the exception message. Tool-call failures add the error name and the existing untrusted-data wrapper, but still omit the status.

### Minimal example

From a built n8n checkout:

```sh
cd packages/@n8n/agents
pnpm build
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { McpClient } from './dist/index.js';

for (const status of [429, 503]) {
  const client = new McpClient([{
    name: 'example',
    url: 'https://example.invalid/mcp',
    transport: 'streamableHttp',
    fetch: async () => new Response('Unavailable', { status }),
  }]);
  await client.listTools();
  console.log(status, client.getConnectionFailures()[0]?.error);
  await client.close();
}
JS
```

The supplied fetch returns synthetic HTTP responses. Both printed errors currently omit their status.

### Expected behavior

Keep the HTTP status in each displayed failure so rate limiting can be distinguished from a service outage. Preserve the original exception, authentication behavior and retries. Do not interpret JSON-RPC codes or SSE network error code `-1` as HTTP statuses.

### Evidence

Reproduced against master `fec3317e` using the actual MCP SDK transport with a synthetic fetch function. No model requests or external server were needed. HTTP 429 and 503 were tested at all three phases. The rejected tool was also passed through the actual `ToolCallRunner`; its model-facing error omitted the status.

The relevant paths are `sdk/mcp-client.ts` and `runtime/tools/tool-call-runner.ts` in `packages/@n8n/agents`. The package version is 0.33.0.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
Confirmed on master. The transport error preserves `code`/`status`, but stringifying via `error.message` drops it before reaching `getConnectionFailures()` and `ToolCallRunner`.

To guard against collisions with JSON-RPC error codes (`-32xxx`) or SSE disconnects (`-1`), a quick range check in `@n8n/agents` before formatting does the trick:

**Patch Preview (First 3 lines of verified fix):**
```typescript
const status = (error as { status?: unknown; code?: unknown })?.status
  ?? (error as { code?: unknown })?.code;

# ... [TRUNCATED — Full production patch & verification steps locked below]
```
